solverDefinition: Exact branching search for a dominating set of size <= K. Repeatedly applies a reduction rule: any undominated vertex with no neighbors (degree 0) must be in the solution, so it is picked immediately without branching. Once no forced vertices remain, branches on the closed neighborhood of the highest-degree undominated vertex, trying each neighbor as the next pick. Terminates successfully when all vertices are dominated, and fails a branch once K picks are exhausted without full domination.
source: Fomin, F. V., Grandoni, F., & Kratsch, D. (2009). A measure & conquer approach for the analysis of exact algorithms. Journal of the ACM (JACM), 56(5), 1–32.
complexity: O(n^(K+1)), n = |nodes|, K = target dominating-set size
